title: Anish Giri controversy explained
transcript: Why is everybody talking about this moment? Well, you see in chess there is a rule called touch move which states that if you touch a piece and you have legal moves available for that piece, you have to move it. Now in this game, Anish Giri reaches for his knight. And it seems like he slightly brushed it with his fingers. But after some more thought, he decides to move a bishop instead. As soon as his opponent sees that, he stops the clock and he calls the arbiter. Anish Giri claims that he did not touch the piece. And so the arbiter checks the footage. The conclusion was that the knight was not touched or if it was touched, it was by accident, which means that Anish was indeed allowed to move something else. But because of all of the fuzz created by this situation, Anish got his mind out of the game, and he requested some extra time to make up for it, but the arbiter declined. But despite that, just a few moves later, Anish's opponent blunders checkmate in one. So I suppose it didn't really matter after all. What do you think?
